title: Pride and Prejudice
description: Elizabeth Bennet has four sisters, a mother determined to marry them off, and a neighbour who seems to think very little of her. Austen’s comedy of manners is also one of the sharpest novels ever written about pride, prejudice and the business of marriage.

title: Frankenstein; or, The Modern Prometheus
description: A young scientist assembles a creature from the dead and abandons it the moment it opens its eyes. Written when Shelley was nineteen, the novel follows creator and creation to the Arctic ice.

title: Moby-Dick; or, The Whale
description: Ishmael signs on to the Pequod and finds himself aboard a ship whose captain has a single purpose. Whaling, metaphysics and a white whale, in prose that goes wherever it likes.

title: From the Earth to the Moon
description: With the Civil War over and nothing left to shoot at, Baltimore’s Gun Club sets out to fire a shell at the Moon, and then three men decide to ride inside it.

title: Around the World in Eighty Days
description: Phileas Fogg wagers half his fortune that he can circle the globe in eighty days, and leaves that evening with his new valet Passepartout and a detective on his heels.

title: The War of the Worlds
description: A cylinder lands on Horsell Common, and within days Martian fighting machines are walking through Surrey. The first great alien-invasion novel, told by a man trying to get home.

title: The Time Machine
description: The Time Traveller returns to dinner with a story about the year 802,701, the Eloi, the Morlocks and the far end of the Earth’s history.

title: A Study in Scarlet
description: Dr Watson, back from Afghanistan and short of money, agrees to share rooms with a man who can tell where he has been from a glance. The first Sherlock Holmes story.

title: The Hound of the Baskervilles
description: A family curse, a death on the moor, and footprints that were not those of a man. Holmes sends Watson to Dartmoor ahead of him, or so Watson believes.

title: Jane Eyre
description: An orphan, a charity school, a position as governess at Thornfield Hall and a master with a locked room on the third floor. Brontë’s heroine narrates her own life with a plainness that still startles.

title: Anna Karenina
description: Two stories run side by side: Anna’s affair with Count Vronsky, which costs her everything, and Levin’s search for a life worth living on his estate.

title: Crime and Punishment
description: A former student in a St Petersburg garret convinces himself that a murder would be justified, commits it, and then has to live inside his own head.

title: The Picture of Dorian Gray
description: A beautiful young man wishes his portrait would age in his place. It does. Wilde’s only novel, with its epigrams intact.

title: Alice’s Adventures in Wonderland
description: Alice follows a white rabbit with a pocket watch down a hole and into a country where the logic is impeccable and none of it makes sense.

title: Dracula
description: Told in letters, diaries and newspaper cuttings: a solicitor’s visit to a castle in Transylvania, a ship that arrives at Whitby with no one alive aboard, and what follows.

title: Adventures of Huckleberry Finn
description: Huck fakes his own death and sets off down the Mississippi on a raft with Jim, who is escaping slavery. Told in Huck’s own voice, which is the point.

title: Mrs Dalloway
description: One June day in London. Clarissa Dalloway buys the flowers herself, and the novel moves through the minds of everyone she passes, and of a man she never meets.

title: The Count of Monte Cristo
description: Edmond Dantès is betrayed on the eve of his wedding and locked in the Château d’If. Fourteen years later he walks out with a fortune, a new name and a list.
